en: The Dyads on the Taints and Things Subject to Taints; The Dyads on Causes.

Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava* (*sāsava*) and is a cause (*hetu*), there arises a state that is neither an *āsava* nor associated with an *āsava* and is not a cause, by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). … three [combinations].

Dependent on a state that is associated with an *āsava* but is not itself an *āsava* and is a cause, there arises a state that is neither an *āsava* nor associated with an *āsava* and is not a cause, by way of the root condition. … one [combination].

Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and associated with an *āsava* and is a cause, and a state that is associated with an *āsava* but is not itself an *āsava* and is a cause, there arises a state that is neither an *āsava*…
And a state that is neither an outflow (*anāsava*) nor a cause (*nahetu*) arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). … One. (Abbreviated.
Under the root condition there are five … pe … under the ripening condition (*vipāka*) there is one … pe … under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are five.

Dependent on a state that is both an outflow (*āsava*) and subject to outflows (*sāsava*), and which is not a cause, a state that is neither an outflow nor subject to outflows and is not a cause arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are five … pe … under the non-disappearance condition there are five.
